textPlacement.assessment: Both Everyday care and Connection & feelings rows retain the conditional wait for a pause. The full entry preserves checking that the child heard, a last turn or saved work, absence of required clock-time understanding, optional choices including children who dislike them, and kind help when departure is necessary. These match PDF119–126 and PDF131–136 without a timer prescription, waiting duration, guaranteed agreement or forced-handling recipe. The 18–24 placement stays within the general toddler scope and supplies no attainment deadline.

Both short topic rows retain time and an adult demonstration when words are insufficient. The full entry matches concise information, showing the location/action, positive wording, gentle no-choice transition language and the shoe humor example across PDF122–126. Processing is presented as a possibility, not a certain explanation of nonresponse or a countdown test; the seven-year-old shoelace anecdote does not become an 18–24-month expectation. There is no imported toileting compulsion or promise that a strategy always works.

The topic row makes adult-supplied ideas explicit for young toddlers. The full entry preserves child input with adult leadership, possible preverbal participation and revisiting a workable plan from PDF119. Its occasional note/picture acknowledgment stays within PDF127, with the PDF166 notebook reuse read as context. Immediate safety action remains explicit through PDF133. The entry adds no child reading requirement, formal meeting, hot-oven sign setup or independence threshold.

Both short rows explain toddler movement/conversation needs and adjusted adult expectations without excusing harmful actions or promising silence. Full detail preserves the specific books, airport-window observation and cafe walk examples and the adult’s possible unavailability for phone/magazine use from PDF125–126 and PDF181. Sensitive small travel objects and screen-health claims are not repackaged as instructions. Ordinary descriptive preparation is valid in the stated toddler browsing band.

The short perspective holds a few clear safety/respect limits together with understanding disappointment. Full detail faithfully includes related consequences, the indoor ball being put away with another chance later, neutral reconsideration of house rules, acknowledged changes of mind, and the checklist’s clarity, kindness, reason and age/ability fit. The entry does not demand repeated explanations, use the older cycling anecdote as toddler practice, or convert consistency into inflexibility or a motive diagnosis. Both cited spans and their full intervening context were read.

The topic row itself retains available comfort, declined touch, protection and calm before explanatory debrief/repair. Full detail matches continued nearby support when a cuddle is declined, immediate action for harm, the four qualified trigger possibilities on PDF138, conditional movement out of the way in public, and gentle help when time requires departure. PDF136’s around-three calm-space passage and PDF138’s over-three recap were read in full and remain outside this 18–24-month entry. There is no required touch, ignoring/withholding comfort, prescribed duration, diagnostic sigh, brain claim or guaranteed prevention.

The topic row independently retains calm first, a small supported role and adult apology modeling without requiring the child to say sorry. Full detail accurately uses gathering thrown items, checking the other person and offering a tissue, preserves adult help and room for the child’s experience, and does not turn the older-child breakfast anecdote into a toddler task. The surrounding reconnection and support unit makes clear that accepting feelings and addressing harm coexist.

The short row leads with close adult protection, keeps understanding alongside protection, and explicitly delays repair until calm. Full detail matches stopping the action/separating when needed, observing patterns and adult responses, and checking on the other person/modeling amends. It does not claim certainty about motive or laughter, prescribe sensory/food/teething/pressure treatment, assess injury, guarantee a phase will pass, or use the adult tea-break example to leave children unsafe. All original prevention-list material and its relevant calming cross-reference were read before accepting this narrower attributed description.

Both Connection & feelings and Play & discovery rows retain observation, protection and an appropriate outlet. Full detail accurately retains moving vulnerable items, temporary removal of objects that can hurt including wooden toys, and the original distinction between throwing outside and soft indoor possibilities on PDF176. PDF132 supplies the related limit/try-later context. The entry does not promise all throwing ends spontaneously or turn socks/beanbags into an unsourced size, construction or blanket safety recommendation.

Both short rows retain company, shared play/work and attention to needed help. Full detail presents temperament, change, divided attention and skill difficulty as possibilities; keeps shared play before increased watching, ordinary laundry participation, supervision and the absence of hours-long solo-play expectations; and preserves orientation plus announced departures. It does not diagnose a motive, use metaphors as child types, require solitary play, prescribe departure intervals, or promise increasing distance on a schedule.

The short row restricts the shoulder-hand example to ordinary conversation and includes the adult acknowledgment and return at a pause. Full detail accurately describes the adult’s hand over the child’s, listening as soon as appropriate, practice and no specified waiting duration from PDF171–172. The immediate-protection reference prevents the signal from becoming a prerequisite for urgent help. The adjoining around-2.5-year peer-play sentence was not imported as this signal’s age or readiness threshold.
